title: Nonvanishing of products of independent primitive degree-one elements
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $H=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}H^n$ be a nonnegatively graded unital associative $k$-algebra with $H^0=k\cdot1$ and $1\ne0$. Give $H\otimes_kH$ the signed multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg b\deg c}ac\otimes bd$ on homogeneous tensors. Suppose $\Delta:H\to H\otimes_kH$ is a degree-preserving coassociative unital $k$-algebra homomorphism for this multiplication. For every $r\geq0$ and every linearly independent family $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in H^1$ satisfying $\Delta(x_i)=x_i\otimes1+1\otimes x_i$, the ordered product $x_1\cdots x_r\in H^r$ is nonzero. The empty product is $1$. No characteristic restriction or assumption that the squares $x_i^2$ vanish is imposed.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, degree-one nonvanishing ingredient for the Hopf bound. Agent-supplied elementary tensor-coordinate replacement for the invoked Borel structure theorem; it proves only the primitive-product assertion, not the full structure theorem.

proof.text: Induct on $r$, uniformly over all independent primitive families in $H^1$. For $r=0$ the product is $1\ne0$. For $r\ge1$, the prefix $x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1}$ is independent: a relation on the prefix extends by coefficient zero at $x_r$. The induction hypothesis therefore gives $y=x_1\cdots x_{r-1}\ne0$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55: agent-written elementary replacement for only the primitive-product ingredient of the Borel argument.

proof.text: Let $P=(\bigoplus_{n\ne1}H^n)+\operatorname{span}_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})\subseteq H$. Then $x_r\notin P$: projection onto degree one would otherwise express $x_r$ as a linear combination of the preceding independent vectors. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-map-extension-prescribed-value] with $V=H$, $U=k$, $f=0$ on $P$, $v=x_r$, and $u=1$. This gives $\lambda:H\to k$ vanishing on all degrees other than one, with $\lambda(x_i)=0$ for $i<r$ and $\lambda(x_r)=1$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55: agent-written elementary replacement for only the primitive-product ingredient of the Borel argument.

proof.text: Put $z=x_1\cdots x_r$. Multiplicativity and primitivity give $\Delta(z)=\prod_{i=1}^r(x_i\otimes1+1\otimes x_i)$. Distribute this ordered product. For each subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ the term is $(-1)^{N(S)}x_{S^c}\otimes x_S$, with each subproduct in increasing order and $N(S)=\#\{(i,j):i\in S,\ j\notin S,\ i<j\}$. Indeed adjoining a right-hand factor adds no crossing; adjoining a left-hand factor contributes $(-1)^{|S|}$ by the stipulated signed multiplication. This verifies the expansion by induction over the factors, starting with $1\otimes1$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55: agent-written elementary replacement for only the primitive-product ingredient of the Borel argument.

proof.text: The bilinear map $(a,b)\mapsto\lambda(b)a$ induces a linear map $T:H\otimes_kH\to H$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Apply it to the expansion. If $|S|\ne1$, then $x_S$ has degree $|S|$, so $\lambda(x_S)=0$. If $S=\{i\}$ with $i<r$, it also vanishes. The sole surviving term is $S=\{r\}$, whose crossing number is zero; hence $T(\Delta(z))=y\ne0$. Were $z=0$, linearity of $\Delta$ and $T$ would give $T(\Delta(z))=0$, a contradiction. This proves the induction step. All coefficients used here are $0,1,-1$, so the argument also holds in characteristic two.
